## Chaos Clock: The Steampunk Spellshaper

_more commonly known simply as "Chaos Clock"_

No other design of mine has spread farther and been seen by more people than the "Chaos Clock" symbol fractal. Among other awards, it was awarded DeviantArt's "Daily Deviation" and now appears on at least three book covers in full, with multiple other book covers and album art in partial form. It's been part of hundreds of collaborations, including my own "Memento Mori" collab with GreatJester seen here on the right. Simply put, it's now legendary. Iconic.

My very first book cover was for _"[The Manifestation of Hidden Forces](rem)"_ by Anna Czímer, which featured the design right on the front cover and my name on the back of the book. Not only did it then also appear on the cover for the sequel, but spread to _"[Days and Times of Power](days-and-times-of-power)"_ by Eric & Katrina Rasbold. You can see a handful of its other appearances [here in my other cover art](cover-art-others).

Just when I thought it could not spread farther, my friend Sophie showed up to a sync with an AI-generated background... and it included my "Chaos Clock" front and center. I cracked up, sharing links with her to the book covers. It appears the machine armies have also picked up the design. That means it will likely outlive humanity itself as a tokenized part of the memetic flame that already covers the planet.

texts: ## Hyperspace + Spacetime As time and space are not separate, but a continuum through multiple dimensions, then it goes to say that traveling through space would be controlled by a clock. I'm not alone in the fact that imagery of hyperspace -- no matter the form it takes -- hypnotizes me and holds me in awe. Can you imagine? Oh how I would love to stand near the front of a spacecraft as the fabric of spacetime itself is warped and bent all around me and the vessel on which I ride. I'll likely need to wait another lifetime or two for that one. Here in the "Chaos Clock" I've created the control unit to move through hyperspace. This goes in both directions, however... in fact, in all directions. That means the warping through spacetime causes the clock itself to be distorted, so that the quantum afterimage is seen of different paths the clock has taken through the multiverse on various nearby layers... leaving the viewer with these images burned into their retinas from the light and distortion itself. For a while, I tried to track everywhere the design was used. That's where feature journals like [here on DeviantArt](https://www.deviantart.com/jayaprime/journal/A-Touch-of-Chaos-and-Gratitude-641997663) and also [here on DeviantArt](https://www.deviantart.com/jayaprime/journal/Hidden-Forces-Music-Fractal-Chaos-322002784) came from. I've lost track over the years. The original remains [here on DeviantArt](https://www.deviantart.com/jayaprime/art/Fractal-Stock-Chaos-Clock-288004672) and, now that it's been trained into AI for generative art, I've put it into the public domain where it now resides [here on Wikimedia](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Chaos_Clock_-_The_Steampunk_Spell-Shaper.jpg). Before closing this out, I want to shout out one other place where it made an appearance. I really enjoyed the article _"__Embracing The Transience"_ by Runjhun Noopur ([Medium](https://runjhunnoopur.medium.com/embracing-the-transience-4f90c5f99c43)). Reading it felt like coming across a long, lost letter from a kindred soul. \[[Chaos Clock as Prints + More on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/20967488)\] * * * ### Extended Exploration If you've enjoyed my "Chaos Clock" then you really should check out my [pop art fractals](other-pop-art), as well as my [surreal fractalscapes](other-fractalscapes). This design appears in my "[Spectral Iteration](spectral-iteration)" fractal book, as well as on the cover of "[R.E.M](rem)" and "[Days and Times of Power](days-and-times-of-power)".
